summary.oneLiner: Kotak Mahindra Bank is India's largest private sector bank by balance sheet, operating as a diversified, 100%-subsidiary-owned financial conglomerate spanning banking, capital markets, asset management, and protection.
summary.business: Kotak Mahindra Bank provides a comprehensive suite of financial solutions across customer segments and geographies in India, anchored by four interconnected engines: Banking & Lending, Capital Markets, Asset Management, and Protection. The Group serves over 5.2 crore customers through a physical network of 5,581 locations and digital platforms, targeting HNIs, SMEs, Core India retail, and institutional clients. All subsidiaries are 100% beneficially owned by the Bank, enabling integrated product manufacturing and distribution while retaining full profitability within the Group.

risks.risk: Credit Risk â Asset Quality Deterioration
risks.note: Credit risk is the most significant risk for the Group, arising from potential failure of borrowers or counterparties to meet obligations. Deterioration in repayment capacity, sector stress, or macroeconomic shocks could impair asset quality and profitability.

RBI reduced the policy repo rate by 100 basis points during the year, leading to NIM compression across the banking sector. Sustained low-rate environment or competitive pricing pressure could further compress margins.

Regulatory constraints that had restricted certain digital onboarding and credit card business activities were lifted only in February 2025. Future regulatory actions or non-compliance could again restrict business capacity or impose penalties.

risks.risk: Data Security and Privacy / Cyber Risk
risks.note: Increasing reliance on digital channels and data-driven operations heightens exposure to cyber threats, data breaches, and service disruptions, which can lead to regulatory penalties, reputational damage, and loss of customer trust.

Inadequate integration of climate and ESG risks in lending and investment decisions may affect credit quality and portfolio resilience. The Bank strengthened its Environmental and Social risk framework during the year, embedding it into credit decisions.

Credit risk concentration is actively managed to prevent excessive exposure to individual borrowers, groups, sectors, or geographies. Breach of concentration limits could amplify losses in a downturn.

The Group maintains prudent buffers above regulatory minima, but adverse macroeconomic scenarios or unexpected losses could strain capital adequacy, requiring capital conservation or constraining growth.

The Group serves over 5.2 crore customers through a physical network of 5,581 locations and digital platforms, targeting HNIs, SMEs, Core India retail, and institutional clients. All subsidiaries are 100% beneficially owned by the Bank, enabling integrated product manufacturing and distribution while retaining full profitability within the Group.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:

Entity renamed Zurich Kotak General Insurance Company India Limited.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Banking & Lending:** Kotak811 (digital banking), Solitaire (HNI proposition), Private Bank, SME Banking, Corporate Bank, Tractor Finance, Commercial Vehicles Finance, Construction Equipment Finance, Mortgage Loans
- **Capital Markets:** Investment Banking (KMCC), Institutional Equities, Broking (Kotak Securities), Kotak Neo (trading app)
- **Asset Management:** Domestic Mutual Funds (Debt & Equity), Offshore Funds, Alternate Assets, PMS, NPS
- **Protection:** Life Insurance (Kotak Mahindra Life Insurance)

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- India (pan-India, metro/urban/semi-urban/rural)
- International (NRI, institutional clients via GIFT City, DIFC Dubai, New York, London, Mauritius, Singapore, Abu Dhabi)

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Global uncertainty, geopolitical tensions and volatile business sentiment resulted in muted corporate credit demand in H1 FY26; activity improved in H2, particularly across wholesale trade, commercial real estate and lending to NBFCs.
- In an environment where the benchmark repo rate fell sharply, profitability was supported by pricing discipline and deeper participation in non-credit businesses.
- Sustained momentum in new business origination while maintaining stable spreads drove Corporate SME growth of 16.67% YoY.
- Healthy working capital demand across sectors supported Business Banking growth of 23.98% YoY.
- Deeper customer engagement, cross-sell, higher fee income and continued New-to-Bank acquisitions drove Agri SME growth of 15.43% YoY.
- Tractor industry grew 23.47% supported by favourable policy measures, subsidy support and positive monsoon conditions; the Bank pursued calibrated growth relative to industry momentum.
- Commercial Vehicles industry grew approximately 13% in unit terms, supported by GST-related pricing benefits and pre-buying ahead of anticipated OEM price revisions.
- Subdued offshore flows amid volatility were partly offset by strong domestic participation in the custody business.
- Credit substitute portfolio moderated in favour of the advances book reflecting interest rate movements in the market.
- Japan and Taiwan desks continued to build a strong pipeline for multinational companies.
- Real Estate Financing sustained momentum in new originations, supported by deep relationships with established developers and a diversified exposure profile, adding new-to-bank clients to strengthen the future pipeline.
- Syndication and Debt Capital Markets delivered healthy growth in debt placements and recorded fee income at an all-time high for the second consecutive year, with regulatory permission for acquisition financing expanding addressable opportunity meaningfully.
- Asset Reconstruction Division actively tracking opportunities across corporate and retail segments.

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Build a unified digital SME platform spanning sourcing, underwriting, credit and operations to improve turnaround time, operational efficiency and customer experience.
- Shift Corporate Banking toward a diversified, capital-efficient model by reducing reliance on spread-based income and scaling fee-based, transaction and flow-driven revenues.
- Prioritise granular, diversified growth in the Mid-Market segment, significantly faster than other segments, driven by new-to-bank customer additions and referral-led sourcing.
- Leverage Centres of Excellence for large corporates (Infrastructure Financing, Real Estate Financing, Financial Institutions, Financial Sponsors, Multi-National Companies, New-age Companies Banking) to deliver expertise and healthy profitability.
- Scale fee-led, capital-efficient niche businesses (Syndication & Debt Capital Markets, Custody Services, Asset Reconstruction) to enhance earnings quality and diversification beyond lending.
- Strengthen transaction banking franchise by deepening participation in customer flows through trade finance, supply chain solutions and cash management services.
- Execute a geography-led expansion strategy in Tractor and Farm Equipment, combining consolidation in mature markets with selective growth in underpenetrated regions.
- Deepen engagement with the venture capital ecosystem for early access to funded startups and maintain a fast-tracked credit framework for portfolio companies of leading VC firms.
- The Board proposed a dividend for the year ended 31st March, 2026, payable after shareholder approval at the Annual General Meeting. The Bank also executed a sub-division (split) of equity shares from face value of ₹5 to ₹1 effective 14th January, 2026, reflecting a shareholder-friendly capital management approach.
- Strengthened Environmental and Social (E&S) risk framework during the year, aligning with global standards and embedding it into credit decisions through policy enhancements and training.
- Embed ESG and climate risk assessment in credit processes, scenario analysis, and portfolio monitoring to enhance portfolio resilience.
- Reasonable Assurance obtained on BRSR Core as per SEBI guidelines; Limited assurance on additional select indicators.
- CSR applicable under Section 135 of Companies Act, 2013; community grievances received through NGO partners with no grievances reported in the period.
- Women representation on Board of Directors at 16.7% and in Key Management Personnel at 16.7%; permanent employee female representation at 32.2%.
- Differently abled permanent employees represent 85.3% male and 14.7% female of the differently abled employee base.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The annual report does not describe specific new capacity, plant, or infrastructure expansion projects with commissioning timelines. The narrative focuses on scaling the franchise through organic growth in advances and deposits, supported by technology enhancements and the lifting of regulatory constraints on digital onboarding and credit card activities. The three strategic pillars—Focus Customer Segment Propositions, Independent Product Businesses within the Bank, and Technology, Digital & AI—are now fully aligned to enable seamless execution. Growth is led by SME, Mortgage, and Corporate Banking segments, with ongoing investments in technology and digital capabilities to support scalability.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- 100% ownership of all subsidiaries ensures complete strategic alignment, governance control, and retention of entire embedded value/profitability within the Group across cycles.
- Diversified four-engine conglomerate model (Banking, Capital Markets, Asset Management, Protection) provides inherent counter-cyclical resilience and earnings stability.
- Strong capital position with standalone CET-1 ratio of 21.34% and consolidated CAR of 22.97%, providing strategic flexibility.
- Established brand and robust governance/risk management framework built over four decades, evidenced by 5-year BVPS CAGR of 16%.
- Integrated distribution combining physical branches evolving into 'One Kotak' destinations with digital and voice-assisted channels, enabling cross-selling and advisory-led engagement.
- Deep domain expertise in niche lending segments: ranked #2 in Tractor Finance and among top five in Commercial Vehicles and Construction Equipment finance.
